articles.title: Rogan warns of youth support for communism as comic Yakov Smirnoff recalls escape from USSR
articles.summary: Joe Rogan slammed young Americans' growing push toward communism during a powerful conversation with Yakov Smirnoff about escaping the Soviet Union.
articles.body:
Comedian Yakov Smirnoff shared his experience of secretly listening to Voice of America in the USSR and escaping to the U.S. with his family through a deal involving Soviet emigration and U.S. grain.

Podcaster Joe Rogan expressed frustration over the push towards communism among young Americans, warning of the dangers of government control and the need for a more ethical version of capitalism.

Former RNC national spokesperson Elizabeth Pipko emphasized the importance of stories like Smirnoff's in highlighting the dangers of communism and the need to protect America's freedom and ideals.

Podcaster Joe Rogan blasted what he described as a "push towards communism" among young Americans as he spoke to legendary comedian Yakov Smirnoff, who grew up in the USSR.

Smirnoff, a Soviet-born comedian who became popular in the U.S. in the 1980s, described to Rogan how he and his father would secretly listen to Voice of America, a U.S. government-funded international news broadcaster, late at night, knowing that they would get in trouble if anybody knew.

He also described how his mother was greatly concerned over what might happen if others found out that they were yearning for America.

Later in life, after working aboard cruise ships, he proposed that he and his family leave the USSR and apply for a visa to the U.S., and he recalled his mother warned that they might face repercussions if they did so, warning that it would be like "you're going to go through hell."

"And my dad said, 'Yeah, we will.' And she said, 'Well, if you're willing to do it, so am I,'" Smirnoff recalled.

Smirnoff said the process of getting a visa to America was only possible because of a deal involving the Carter administration, Soviet emigration and U.S. grain.

"[Carter] wanted to see some human rights in the Soviet Union. And the Soviet leadership was — they were starving. They didn't have food. So, they needed food from America. So, Jimmy Carter made a deal that we're going to give you grain, and you allow people to get out, and that's how we were kind of exchanged for some wheat, you know," he said. "That's how we got out."

"Wow. Holy s---, man … you sometimes need to be reminded how fortunate you are," Rogan said of Americans like himself. "You know, Americans in particular, we're very, you know, it's not our fault. You know, people become accustomed to where they live. … And they think this is normal, which is one of the reasons why this push towards communism amongst young people is so infuriating to me."

Rogan said he understood why some people might be drawn to socialism out of a sense of "empathy" and the contrast between "people that are so rich and people that are so poor."

"But the solution is not to make the government decide who gets what because they never decide the right way," he warned.

"They do what people do," Rogan warned of communist officials. "What people do when they have power is they enact total control over the population so that they can maintain power, and then they live in luxury. And then you wait in line for bread, and that's how it is all over the f---ing world.

"And if you step out of line, they shoot you. That's where communism goes. So, what we need is, like, a more, a more moral and ethical version of capitalism."

Elizabeth Pipko, a former RNC national spokesperson and the daughter of immigrants from the Soviet Union, spoke to Fox News Digital about the exchange and her family having escaped from the USSR .

"I'm especially moved by his story because it is so incredibly similar to my own family's," she said. "My grandfather told me many times about the secret radio he kept hidden inside a pillowcase, where he and my young mother would listen to Voice of America. Living in the Soviet Union, they would listen and dream of a better life, never knowing that one day America would deliver on those dreams and more.

"I hope people understand that stories like this are incredibly special, but they are not unique," Pipko continued. "For generations, America has been a beacon of freedom and hope to people around the world, including millions who suffered under the horrors of communism. America has defeated communism before — both in reality and in spirit — and will continue to do so until the bitter end."

"I have the privilege of being the daughter of two immigrants, which means I learned very early on just how blessed I am to have been born in the greatest country on the face of the earth, no matter how many misinformed college students tell you otherwise," she said.

"We have a duty to protect what so many came here searching for and to keep our country free from the ideology that they escaped," Pipko added. "Not only for those who fought and died for this nation, but for the millions around the world who still look to America and know that, as long as she shines, anything is possible."

Daniel Di Martino, a Manhattan Institute fellow and economist who fled Venezuela, told Fox News Digital, "Yakov recounts what all of us who have lived under socialism go through in suffering and censorship. And Rogan perfectly describes how socialism is bad for us because it is tyrannical and impoverishing.

"What's most interesting to me, though, is that Rogan himself fell in the past for the allure of socialism that he criticizes by supporting Bernie Sanders in 2020, who himself praised and vacationed in the Soviet Union," he added. "Any nation can fall for the lies of socialists and self-destroy, and we must do everything we can to prevent it."

articles.title: Motivational quote of the day by Mariah Carey: ‘When you feel like hope is gone, look inside you and be strong’ a powerful life lesson to look within, stay hopeful and find the courage to keep going
articles.summary: Discover the profound message behind Mariah Carey's quote from 'Hero', encouraging self-trust and resilience during tough times.
articles.body: When hope starts to fade, perspectives change, often not in the right direction. In those situations, it can be easy to look outside ourselves for answers or motivation. Mariah Carey’s words take a different approach. Her words encourage people to trust themselves when life feels unsettled. You do not always need to know exactly what comes next to find the courage to move forward. At times, simply deciding not to give up can be enough to get you through an uncertain moment.Today’s quote of the day by Mariah Carey reads: “When you feel like hope is gone, look inside you and be strong.”What does the quote by Mariah Carey mean?The line is featured in Carey’s 1993 hit ‘Hero,’ which appears on her album ‘Music Box’. The song was written by Carey and Walter Afanasieff and went on to become one of her signature songs. Carey’s message is about looking inward when life becomes difficult. Losing hope can make a person believe that they need someone else to come along and solve everything, but the quote suggests a different outlook.The idea fits closely with the message of ‘Hero’. Instead of presenting strength as something extraordinary, the song focuses on the part of a person that continues moving forward despite fear or uncertainty. That does not mean people should face every problem alone. Reaching out to friends, family or people we trust is also important. The message is about remembering that outside support does not take away from our own ability to cope, grow and begin again.Why does Mariah Carey’s quote still matter today?Things do not always unfold the way we imagine, and sometimes a sudden setback can leave us wondering what to do next. Career disappointments, personal struggles and uncertainty can all affect confidence. That is why the idea behind Carey’s quote continues to feel relevant. It encourages people not to judge their entire future by one difficult moment.Hope does not always have to mean believing that everything will immediately become perfect. At times, getting through a difficult phase is simply about trusting yourself enough to keep going. Carey’s message also points toward believing in your own abilities, especially when things around you are beyond your control. Changing a situation might not be an answer every time, but you can decide how you face it. Even that small change in mindset can make it easier to rebuild confidence and take the next step.Early life of Mariah CareyBorn on March 27, 1969, in New York, Mariah Carey had music around her from the beginning. Her mother, Patricia Carey, worked as a voice coach and opera singer, so music was already a big part of Mariah’s childhood. She began singing lessons when she was only four, and over the years, her voice grew into the five-octave range that later became one of her most recognisable strengths.After finishing high school in 1987, Carey headed to Manhattan with dreams of making it in music. The early days were not glamorous. She took on different jobs to make ends meet, while using whatever free time she had to write songs and work on demos. She also performed as a backing vocalist for singer Brenda K. Starr, contributing supporting vocals during the early stage of her career.Her determination eventually led to a breakthrough. At 18, Carey had a demo tape that reached Columbia Records executive Tommy Mottola after she attended a record-industry party with Starr. Mottola listened to the tape and subsequently signed her.How did Mariah Carey rise to fame?Carey launched her recording career with her self-titled debut album in 1990. The record quickly established her as a major new voice, helped by songs including ‘Vision of Love’ and ‘Love Takes Time’. Her second album, Emotions, followed in 1991.Her breakthrough continued with Music Box in 1993. The album included ‘Dreamlover’, ‘Without You’ and ‘Hero’, with the latter becoming one of the defining songs of her career. Apple Music lists Music Box as a 1993 album and includes ‘Hero’ among its tracks.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. Download the TOI app.Give your child the gift of confidence! articles.title: Pérola encontrada em salgado em SP: saiba o valor real da joia | G1
articles.standfirst: Esfera encontrada em Cananéia (SP) não passou por avaliação gemológica. Especialistas apontam que ela ainda está em formação; entenda quais critérios determinam o valor.
articles.summary: A pérola encontrada em um salgado de ostra em Cananéia (SP) pode valer menos de R$ 50, segundo especialistas que analisam a raridade do achado.
articles.body:
A pérola encontrada por uma personal trainer enquanto ela comia um salgado feito com ostra em Cananéia, no litoral de São Paulo, talvez nem ultrapasse os R$ 50, segundo o biólogo Ricardo Samelo, ouvido pelo g1 . Para ele, porém, a raridade das circunstâncias do achado chama mais atenção do que o possível valor da peça.

A pequena esfera não passou por uma avaliação gemológica, mas profissionais ouvidos pela reportagem apontam, a partir das imagens, indícios de que seja uma pérola irregular ainda em formação. Para determinar o valor de um exemplar, são considerados critérios específicos, que incluem tamanho, formato, cor e lustre.

O caso aconteceu no domingo (20), depois que Carina Lisboa, de 41 anos, e o aluno Jordinei Francisca pararam para almoçar após uma caminhada . A personal havia sido convidada pela proprietária do restaurante Ponto das Ostras, no Centro da cidade, para experimentar um novo prato preparado com a ostra exótica Saccostrea cucullata.

Após analisar imagens do achado, Samelo explicou que a esfera apresenta características de uma pérola barroca, nome dado às pérolas de formato irregular. "As pérolas irregulares são chamadas de pérolas barrocas e não costumam ser caras. Uma única pérola talvez nem ultrapasse R$ 50", afirmou.

O valor de uma pérola, no entanto, não pode ser definido apenas pelo formato. O Gemological Institute of America (GIA), instituto norte-americano especializado em pesquisa e avaliação de gemas, estabelece sete fatores para determinar o valor geral de pérolas naturais ou cultivadas e de joias.

Pérola foi encontrada em um prato servido em um restaurante de Cananéia — Foto: Arquivo Pessoal

De acordo com o GIA, os sete fatores considerados são:

Tamanho: quando as demais características são equivalentes, pérolas maiores são mais raras e valiosas do que as menores do mesmo tipo;

Formato: entre as cultivadas, a redonda é a mais difícil de produzir e, em condições equivalentes, geralmente a mais valiosa. Pérolas barrocas, porém, também podem ser valorizadas;

Cor: são consideradas a cor predominante e outras tonalidades e efeitos visuais. Oferta, procura, moda e tradições culturais também podem influenciar o valor;

Lustre: corresponde à qualidade da reflexão da luz e pode ser, segundo o GIA, o mais importante dos sete fatores;

Superfície: riscos, rugas e outras irregularidades podem reduzir o valor quando são numerosas ou intensas;

Nácar: a qualidade das camadas que formam a pérola está diretamente relacionada ao lustre e também influencia a durabilidade;

Uniformidade: considerada principalmente em joias com mais de uma pérola, avalia o quanto elas combinam em características como tamanho, formato, cor e lustre.

Pérola encontrada dentro de ostra durante o passeio — Foto: Flávia Mantovani/G1

O termo "barroca" é usado para descrever pérolas de formato irregular. Portanto, essa característica, sozinha, não determina quanto um exemplar vale.

O GIA explica que, entre as pérolas cultivadas, as redondas são mais raras e geralmente mais valiosas quando os demais fatores são equivalentes. O instituto ressalta, porém, que exemplares barrocos bem formados também podem ser valorizados.

No caso da esfera encontrada por Carina, não houve uma avaliação gemológica para determinar o valor ou classificá-la formalmente. A partir das imagens, especialistas ouvidos pelo g1 apontaram características compatíveis com uma pérola irregular ainda em formação.

Para Samelo, a peculiaridade do episódio está principalmente nas circunstâncias do achado.

"O evento se torna interessante mais pela raridade. Encontrar uma pérola enquanto se alimenta de uma ostra é algo inusitado, fato que certamente será lembrado para sempre pelas pessoas envolvidas. Não se trata de valor, e sim de uma história para contar", afirmou o biólogo.

Os biólogos Alex Ribeiro e Ricardo Samelo explicaram ao g1 que as pérolas são formadas por um mecanismo de defesa de moluscos bivalves, como ostras e mexilhões.

Segundo Samelo, o processo começa quando um corpo estranho invade o organismo e é isolado pelo animal com um revestimento que recebe novas camadas ao longo do tempo.

O GIA explica que o nácar é uma substância produzida por determinados moluscos e depositada em camadas durante a formação da pérola. A interação da luz com essas camadas contribui para os efeitos ópticos característicos das pérolas.

Nas pérolas cultivadas, o processo é iniciado intencionalmente pelo ser humano. Dependendo da técnica, pode ser introduzido no molusco um pequeno pedaço de tecido do manto ou um núcleo acompanhado desse tecido, dando início ao mesmo processo biológico envolvido na formação das pérolas naturais.

Carina sentiu algo duro ao morder o salgado e, inicialmente, pensou que tivesse quebrado um dente. "Dei uma mordida e senti uma coisa dura. Eu falei: 'Nossa, acho que quebrei o meu dente, deve ter um pedaço de ostra aqui dentro'. Aí comecei a mexer e vi que tinha uma bolinha, que não tinha sido dente", relembrou.

O prato havia sido criado para o 1º Festival GastroMangue, promovido pela prefeitura com apoio da Universidade Estadual Paulista (Unesp). A iniciativa propôs a criação de receitas com a Saccostrea cucullata, espécie originária da Ásia e considerada invasora por disputar espaço com espécies nativas na região.

A proprietária do restaurante, Paula Monteiro, afirmou que foi a primeira vez que um cliente encontrou uma esfera semelhante a uma pérola em 18 anos de comércio. Carina pretende transformar o achado em um brinco de ponto de luz.

articles.title: Coronel que enfrentou cangaceiro de Lampião inspira peça premiada    | G1
articles.standfirst: Obra 'Até que tu te tornes verde", do Teatro do Kaos, de Cubatão (SP), é baseado nas memórias familiares do ator Lourimar Vieira e venceu como Melhor Espetáculo pelos júris oficial e popular em festival nacional no Piauí.
articles.summary: Obra 'Até que tu te tornes verde", do Teatro do Kaos, de Cubatão (SP), é baseado nas memórias familiares do ator Lourimar Vieira e venceu como Melhor Espetáculo.
articles.body:
Coronel que enfrentou cangaceiro de Lampião inspira peça de SP que conquista sete prêmios — Foto: Divulgação

O espetáculo 'Até que tu te tornes verde', do Teatro do Kaos, de Cubatão (SP), conquistou sete prêmios no 14º Festival Nacional de Teatro do Piauí, realizado entre os dias 16 e 23 de setembro, em Floriano (PI).

A companhia esteve entre os 20 finalistas do festival, que reuniu produções de 13 estados brasileiros. O grupo cubatense recebeu prêmios pelo espetáculo e pelo trabalho de atores e profissionais envolvidos na montagem.

O Teatro do Kaos conquistou sete prêmios no festival:

Melhor Espetáculo pelo júri oficial: Teatro do Kaos;

Melhor Espetáculo pelo júri popular: Teatro do Kaos;

Melhor Ator Coadjuvante: Fabiano di Melo;

A companhia também foi finalista em outras cinco categorias: Melhor Texto, Melhor Atriz, Melhor Ator Coadjuvante, Melhor Iluminação e Melhor Trilha Sonora.

A montagem parte das memórias de Lourimar Vieira, fundador do Teatro do Kaos e um dos atores do espetáculo. Nascido em Oeiras (PI), ele levou ao palco lembranças do avô, o coronel Liberato (1884-1975).

Na peça, o coronel é retratado como uma figura respeitada e temida, que mediava conflitos entre moradores e julgava determinadas situações. A montagem também aborda episódios como um confronto com Zé Corisco, apresentado no espetáculo como integrante do bando de Lampião.

O envelhecimento do coronel também faz parte da narrativa, que aborda temas como perda de memória, confusão mental e solidão. Para Lourimar, a premiação teve um significado especial por representar um retorno às próprias origens.

"Foi uma emoção muito grande poder retornar ao meu estado e ainda conquistar este prêmio. O teatro faz com que você aceite quem você é e que tenha orgulho de suas origens", afirmou.

A próxima apresentação de 'Até que tu te tornes verde' está prevista para 17 de dezembro, no Sesc Santos. Antes disso, Lourimar pretende levar o espetáculo e outras produções da companhia ao Teatro Zanzalá, em Cubatão.

articles.title: Imagineland 2026: Último dia em Campina Grande tem One Piece e K-pop | G1
articles.standfirst: Último dia do evento terá atrações como Lera Abova, de "One Piece: A Série", e o ator e cantor sul-coreano Lee Jin-hyuk, além de painéis, exibições e atividades para o público.
articles.summary: O Imagineland 2026 encerra a programação em Campina Grande com Lera Abova e Lee Jin-hyuk, reunindo fãs de One Piece e K-pop neste domingo.
articles.body:
Último dia do evento terá atrações como Lera Abova, de 'One Piece: A Série', e o ator e cantor sul-coreano Lee Jin-hyuk — Foto: Montagem/g1

O Imagineland On The Road 2026 , evento geek com vários artistas internacionais, chega ao fim neste domingo (27), em Campina Grande . A programação do dia conta com atrações como a atriz Lera Abova, de "One Piece: A Série" , e o ator e cantor sul-coreano Lee Jin-hyuk .

Entre os destaques do Imagineland 2026 estiveram Corbin Bleu , Lucas Grabeel e Monique Coleman , do elenco de "High School Musical", que participaram das comemorações dos 20 anos do primeiro filme. Também passaram pelo evento o ator Zach Roerig, de "The Vampire Diaries" , e Walter Jones, de "Power Rangers" .

A programação também conta com painéis com dubladores, exibição de filmes, séries e animes, atrações de K-pop e doramas, torneios de games, luta medieval e espaços para quadrinistas e artistas.

As atividades são distribuídas em cinco espaços principais: Teatro Shaolin, Red Carpet Claro TV+, Claro Gaming Zone, Artists’ Alley e Arena Medieval. O evento também terá estandes de marcas, praça de alimentação, Arena Dance e Arena Laser Tag.

Os portões são abertos às 11h e o evento segue até às 21h. O passaporte dá acesso aos espaços do Imagineland, com exceção da área de fotos e autógrafos, que é cobrada à parte.

O Imagineland 2026 também tem transporte oficial entre João Pessoa e Campina Grande. O serviço sai do Espaço Cultural José Lins do Rêgo, na capital, a partir das 8h, com retorno previsto para as 21h.

O transporte é vendido separadamente e há opções para um, dois ou os três dias do evento.

Os ingressos para o Imagineland são vendidos pela internet, pelo site oficial do evento.

articles.title: 'Feito Pipa' amplia imaginário do cinema com Sertão colorido | G1
articles.standfirst: André Araújo afirmou que uma das preocupações durante a escrita do filme foi revisitar a forma como o cinema historicamente retrata o Nordeste.
articles.summary: André Araújo afirmou que uma das preocupações durante a escrita do filme foi revisitar a forma como o cinema historicamente retrata o Nordeste.
articles.body:
Representante brasileiro para eventual vaga no Oscar de melhor filme internacional, "Feito Pipa" propõe um olhar diferente sobre o interior do Nordeste . Em vez de imagens associadas à seca e à pobreza, o longa-metragem dirigido pelo cearense Allan Deberton aposta em afeto, cores, memória e música para contar a história de Gugu, menino de 11 anos criado pela avó materna.

Em entrevista ao g1, o roteirista André Araújo afirmou que uma das preocupações durante a escrita foi revisitar a forma como o cinema historicamente retrata o Nordeste.

"Quando estou escrevendo, sempre me preocupo em atualizar as imagens e os imaginários que o cinema produz sobre o Sertão. No 'Feito Pipa', esse Sertão colorido surge como uma forma de se distanciar daquele Sertão que a gente costuma ver da fotografia alaranjada ou da luz estourada, o Sertão da miséria, o Sertão da seca", disse.

Para Araújo, o filme apresenta outras formas de enxergar esse território: "É o colorido que se manifesta através das pessoas, dos personagens, que se manifesta na própria fotografia, na identidade de Gugu, de Dilma, que se apropriam desse universo lúdico para se projetarem no mundo, para serem quem são".

Yuri Gomes, de 11 anos, viveu Gugu no filme "Feito Pipa" (2026) — Foto: Jamille Queiroz

Poucos territórios foram tão revisitados pelo cinema brasileiro quanto o interior nordestino. Ao longo do século XX, a região foi palco de diferentes movimentos e estéticas, desde a fase inaugural, representada por produções como "O Cangaceiro" (1953), de Lima Barreto, até os filmes do Cinema Novo, que transformaram a paisagem sertaneja em símbolo das desigualdades sociais brasileiras, sobretudo através da obra do cineasta baiano Glauber Rocha, com destaque para “Deus e o Diabo na Terra do Sol” (1964).

Para a pesquisadora paulista Eliana Guerra, que faz doutorado em História da Arte na Universidade de Salamanca, na Espanha, o Sertão ocupa uma posição singular na cinematografia brasileira por ser um território que ela considera simbólico.

"Ao longo da história do nosso cinema, ele foi construído e representado a partir de questões muito profundas da sociedade brasileira, como a desigualdade, os conflitos pela terra, a religiosidade, a violência e as migrações, mas também os afetos, os modos de vida e diferentes formas de existência", afirma.

Segundo ela, o próprio cinema participa da construção do imaginário sobre a região: "Durante muito tempo, determinadas representações acabaram associando esse território principalmente à seca, à pobreza, à violência e ao cangaço. Mas o cinema brasileiro também foi transformando essas imagens e mostrando que existem muitos sertões, com diferentes paisagens, sujeitos, experiências e modos de vida."

A partir dessa pesquisa, Guerra define o Sertão como um "dispositivo estético e político" do cinema brasileiro.

"Ele não funciona apenas como cenário. A paisagem, a luz, os sons, os corpos, os modos de falar e de viver participam da construção dos sentidos da obra. E ele também é político porque escolher como representar o Sertão significa escolher quais sujeitos, histórias e experiências serão vistos e ouvidos", define.

Filme "Feito Pipa", escolhido para representar o Brasil na busca pelo Oscar 2027, tem como cenário o município de Quixadá — Foto: Divulgação

Nas últimas décadas, cineastas passaram a apresentar novas leituras desse território. Obras como "O Céu de Suely" (2006), de Karim Aïnouz; "Bacurau" (2019), de Kleber Mendonça Filho e Juliano Dornelles; e "Paloma" (2022), de Marcelo Gomes , ajudaram a ampliar o repertório de experiências, paisagens e personagens associadas ao interior nordestino, como são os casos dos protagonistas interpretados por Hermila Guedes, Silvério Pereira e Kika Sena, respectivamente.

É nesse contexto de multiplicação dos olhares sobre o interior do Nordeste que "Feito Pipa" pode ser inserido. "São filmes que, cada um à sua maneira, ajudaram a ampliar o imaginário sobre o Sertão e a romper com uma representação muito cristalizada desse lugar no cinema brasileiro", afirma o roteirista do filme, André Araújo.

Entre as referências mais próximas, ele cita especialmente a obra de Aïnouz gravada em Iguatu e "Pacarrete" (2019), obra estrelada pela atriz Marcélia Cartaxo, um longa-metragem rodado em Russas, no Vale do Jaguaribe, que, assim como "Feito Pipa", tem colaboração de Araújo no roteiro e a direção assinada por Deberton.

"O que me interessava era imaginar o Sertão pelo olhar de Gugu: um lugar que pode ser duro e atravessado por contradições, mas que também é colorido, afetivo, fantasioso e cheio de possibilidades. O Sertão do filme não é apenas o cenário onde Gugu vive. É parte da maneira como ele inventa o mundo" , pontua o roteirista.

André Araújo é roteirista de Feito Pipa — Foto: Cedida

As filmagens de "Feito Pipa" foram realizadas em Quixadá, no Sertão Central cearense. A escolha, segundo o roteirista, foi resultado de um estudo de viabilidade.

"Fizemos uma pesquisa de locação em todo o Ceará até chegar a esse município, que conseguia suprir todas as demandas do roteiro em termos de paisagens e questões logísticas", explica.

Mas a origem da história nasceu fora, num estado vizinho, que também compartilha o clima semiárido. Em 2012, Araújo conheceu São Rafael, no interior do Rio Grande do Norte, município conhecido por ter sido parcialmente inundado pelas águas da barragem Armando Ribeiro Gonçalves. Em períodos de estiagem, estruturas da cidade velha emergem, entre elas a torre da igreja, experiência que foi ponto de partida para o roteiro.

"Na época, eu estava fazendo uma pesquisa sobre a cidade antiga que havia reaparecido após 30 anos submersa pela barragem. Aquela imagem da igreja me inspirou a pensar essa história. A cidade que reaparece e as memórias que se apagam. Em 'Feito Pipa', a memória é sobrevivência", afirma André Araújo.

É a mesma cidade que aparece num clássico do cinema realizado no interior do Nordeste: "Cabra Marcado para Morrer" (1984). Em São Rafael, o cineasta Eduardo Coutinho reencontrou Elizabeth Teixeira durante as filmagens do documentário que aborda a luta pela reforma agrária na ditadura militar no Brasil.

Embora com temas distintos, as duas obras demonstram como o Sertão tem sido ressignificado pelo cinema brasileiro. Essa aproximação ganha força com a memória ocupando papel central nas narrativas: se Coutinho documenta uma história interrompida pela repressão política, Araújo e Deberton partem da imagem de uma cidade submersa para construir uma trama em que recordar é uma forma de permanecer.

Filme cearense "Feito pipa" é pré-selecionado para representar o Brasil no Oscar — Foto: Divulgação/Paris Filmes

Em inglês, o filme ganhou o nome de "Gugu's World" ("O Mundo de Gugu", em tradução livre) , como forma de sintetizar a jornada do protagonista: um menino criado pela avó materna que, após descobrir que ela está perdendo a memória, luta para não ir morar com o pai homofóbico, interpretado por Lázara Ramos.

Para o roteirista André Araújo, esse vínculo entre avó e neto é um dos elementos que mais têm emocionado espectadores em diferentes festivais, como Berlim e Gramado.

Segundo ele, a força emocional da história está na universalidade desse afeto: "O amor que une avó e neto é tão verdadeiro, tão íntimo, mas também tão autêntico, divertido, que nem mesmo o Alzheimer consegue apagar. É o fio que permanece para além da memória e do esquecimento. E é o fio que conecta o público com a história".

Outro aspecto central da narrativa é a construção de Gugu como uma criança queer . O roteirista afirma que desejava retratar um personagem marcado não apenas pelos conflitos provocados pela intolerância, mas também pela liberdade característica da infância.

"Quando idealizei Gugu, eu queria que ele fosse radiante, livre, performático, mas, sobretudo, uma criança. Uma criança que ainda não precisa nomear quem é, que experimenta o mundo com liberdade e encontra prazer em ser exatamente como é", comentou.

Para Araújo, a trama desafia a ideia de um Sertão exclusivamente conservador: "Eu queria imaginar outras possibilidades. Um Sertão onde esse menino também pudesse ser livre, amado e feliz, não apesar de quem ele é, mas simplesmente sendo quem é."

Embora ainda não tenha assistido ao longa, a pesquisadora Eliana Guerra afirma acompanhar com interesse a trajetória da produção: "O fato de ter sido filmado em Quixadá e de estabelecer uma relação tão próxima entre os personagens e o território já desperta bastante o meu interesse como pesquisadora."

Para ela, filmes produzidos em diferentes épocas demonstram que não existe uma única imagem da região no audiovisual brasileiro.

"Não existe uma única imagem do Sertão, mas muitos Sertões possíveis no cinema brasileiro", concluiu a pesquisadora.

Representante brasileiro na corrida por uma vaga entre os cinco indicados ao Oscar de Filme Internacional, "Feito Pipa" tem o desafio de repetir a melhor fase do cinema brasileiro , com duas indicações seguidas ao prêmio de melhor filme internacional, "Ainda Estou Aqui" (2024) e "Agente Secreto" (2025), tendo o primeiro conquistado para o Brasil a então inédita estatueta dourada.

Em cartaz em Juazeiro do Norte durante uma semana, o longa teve sessões lotadas. O professor Ribamar Bringel Filho conseguiu assistir ao filme e destaca a canção que é uma das cenas que sintetizam o afeto entre a vó Dilma e neto Gugu.

"A música “Time After Time”, de Cyndi Lauper , transmite justamente essa ideia de estar presente, de permanecer ao lado de alguém, mesmo quando tudo está mudando. No filme, a música reforça a sensação de que o afeto da avó é um porto seguro para o neto. Acho que é isso que torna o filme tão delicado: mostrar que acolher uma criança também é permitir que ela seja livre para descobrir quem é. E que amar é estar por perto, sem impedir que o outro siga seu próprio caminho", destaca.

articles.title: Péricles camufla o potencial vocal em álbum com feats com Ana Castela, Ney Matogrosso, Jota.Pê e Zeca Pagodinho | G1
articles.body:
Péricles lança o álbum 'Camuflagem' com 12 músicas, entre composições inéditas e regravações de canções como 'Faz parte do meu show' — Foto: Rodolfo Magalhães / Divulgação

♬ Péricles lança o álbum “Camuflagem” no rastro do sucesso do show em que cantou o repertório de artistas da gravadora Motown no Rock in Rio 2026. Com 12 músicas, o álbum “Camuflagem” destaca feats do cantor com Ana Castela, Jota.Pê, Ney Matogrosso e Zeca Pagodinho .

Com a boiadeira , Péricles entra no território do pagonejo na gravação da música “Simplesmente acontece” (Guga Capanema, Guilherme Grins e Rayan Felipe). Com Jota.Pê, o dueto acontece na faixa “Até quando” (Daniel Lemos e Leonardo Ferreira), samba-canção que evolui para xote romântico no refrão. A gravação de Péricles com Jota.Pê harmoniza bem os estilos dos dois artistas, sobressaindo no álbum.

Já o encontro de Péricles com Ney Matogrosso rebobina um dos maiores sucessos da discografia solo de Cazuza (1958 – 1990), “Faz parte do meu show” (1988), canção de aura bossa-novista composta por Cazuza em parceria com Renato Ladeira (1952 – 2015).

Em feat fluente com Zeca Pagodinho, o cantor revive “Não quero mais amar a ninguém” (Cartola, Carlos Cachaça e Zé da Zilda, 1936), samba lançado há 90 anos na voz da cantora Aracy de Almeida (1914 – 1988). O dueto é o ponto alto do álbum.

Gravado por Péricles em estúdio com produção musical de Izaías Marcelo e lançado na última sexta-feira, 25 de setembro, o álbum “Camuflagem” também traz no repertório músicas como “Deixei ir” (Prateado e Thiaguinho), “Marcando território” (Elizeu Henrique e Cleitinho Persona), “My love” (Edu Camargo, Fabinho Cézar e Yan Coutinho) e “Tá tudo errado” (Cauíque, Cátia Gonzaga, Filipe Toca e Fábio Braza)

“Tá tudo errado” é o pagode que abre álbum cujo repertório, em muitos momentos, parece camuflar parte das imensas possibilidades de Péricles como cantor porque a maioria das músicas não está à altura da grande voz que seduziu o público do Rock in Rio 2026 ao mergulhar com estilo e propriedade no catálogo da gravadora Motown.

articles.title: Festival Olhar do Norte encerra edição com prêmios no Teatro Amazonas | G1
articles.standfirst: A 8ª edição recebeu 596 inscrições, sendo 28 na Amazônia Longas, 188 na Amazônia Curtas, 325 em Outros Nortes e 55 na Olhinho.
articles.summary: O Festival Olhar do Norte encerra sua 8ª edição com sessões gratuitas e a entrega de 21 troféus no Teatro Amazonas, celebrando o cinema em Manaus.
articles.body:
Festival Olhar do Norte encerra edição com sessões gratuitas, às 18h, será exibida a produção amazonense 'Os Avós'. — Foto: Foto: Divulgação 'Os Avós'

O 8º Festival de Cinema da Amazônia – Olhar do Norte termina neste domingo (27), em Manaus , com duas sessões no Teatro Amazonas e a cerimônia de premiação. A entrada é gratuita. O festival recebeu 596 filmes inscritos. Foram 28 inscrições na Amazônia Longas, 188 na Amazônia Curtas, 325 em Outros Nortes e 55 na Olhinho.

Às 16h, será exibido “Concerto de Quintal”, de Juraci Junior (RO). O filme mostra um músico que revive memórias do pai por meio de gravações em fitas K7 e explora os ritmos que formam a identidade musical de Porto Velho (RO).

Às 18h, o festival encerra as sessões com o longa amazonense “Os Avós”, dirigido por Ana Lígia Pimentel.

A produção retrata a rotina de avós jovens, entre 30 e 35 anos, no Amazonas, e mostra como a antecipação das funções familiares impacta suas vidas.

Para o curador do Olhar do Norte, Diego Bauer, a presença do público ao longo dos cinco dias é um dos destaques desta edição.

Além da plateia do Teatro Amazonas, as sessões no Teatro Gebes Medeiros também atraíram espectadores em diferentes horários, enquanto profissionais do audiovisual participaram das atividades promovidas pelo festival.

“A cada edição, percebemos uma adesão cada vez maior do público ao festival. Tivemos o Teatro Amazonas lotado todos os dias. Isso mostra que existe um público interessado em conhecer e em viver o festival. Chegar ao último dia com essa resposta é muito especial para todos nós”, destaca Diego Bauer.

Neste ano, o festival tem Rhayssa Couto como apresentadora, conduzindo as atividades da programação.

A cerimônia de premiação começa às 20h, no Teatro Amazonas. Serão entregues 21 troféus aos vencedores das quatro mostras competitivas.

Na Mostra Amazônia Longas, serão premiados o “Melhor Filme”, escolhido pelo júri oficial; o “Melhor Filme - Júri Jovem”; e o “Melhor Filme - Voto Popular”.

A Mostra Amazônia Curtas concentra o maior número de categorias. Além de “Melhor Filme”, “Melhor Filme - Júri Jovem” e “Melhor Filme - Voto Popular”, serão entregues os prêmios de “Melhor Direção”, “Melhor Roteiro”, “Melhor Direção de Fotografia”, “Melhor Montagem”, “Melhor Direção de Arte”, “Melhor Som”, “Melhor Figurino” e “Melhor Maquiagem”, além de dois prêmios de “Melhor Atuação” e do “Prêmio Especial do Júri”.

Já nas mostras Olhar Panorâmico e Outros Nortes, serão escolhidos, em cada uma, o “Melhor Filme” pelo júri e o “Melhor Filme - Voto Popular”.

A cerimônia também terá o anúncio do Prêmio Itaú Cultural Play, destinado a um dos filmes da Mostra Amazônia Curtas. O vencedor receberá R$ 15 mil. A escolha é feita exclusivamente pela equipe do Itaú Cultural, considerando critérios de relevância artística e singularidade.

Os filmes das mostras competitivas foram avaliados por profissionais convidados para compor os diferentes júris da oitava edição. Na Mostra Amazônia Longas, o júri é formado por Bea Góes, Christiane Garcia, Miguel Guerrero, Walter Fernandes Jr. e Zienhe Castro. Na Mostra Amazônia Curtas, participam Ana Lígia Pimentel, Anderson Mendes, Denis Lopes e Felippy Damian.

A Mostra Outros Nortes tem como jurados Pâmela Eurídice, Leonardo Barbosa e Marcos Gabriel Farias, enquanto a Mostra Olhar Panorâmico é avaliada por Camila Henriques, Ivanildo Pereira e Mariana Goulão.

O Júri Jovem, responsável pela escolha de “Melhor Filme” nas mostras Amazônia Curtas e Amazônia Longas, é composto por Catharina Hadassa, Janaína Kassandra e Péricles Queiroz.

A oitava edição do Festival de Cinema da Amazônia - Olhar do Norte movimentou Manaus com atividades em diferentes espaços culturais da cidade. A agenda reuniu produções da Amazônia e de outras regiões brasileiras, entre mostras competitivas e não competitivas, além de ações de formação e iniciativas voltadas ao diálogo sobre cinema.

Uma das novidades deste ano foi a estreia da mostra competitiva Amazônia de Longas-metragens, formada por obras realizadas nos estados que integram a Amazônia Legal — Acre, Amapá, Amazonas, Maranhão, Mato Grosso, Pará, Rondônia, Roraima e Tocantins — ou dirigidas por cineastas desses estados.

Também integraram as competições a Amazônia de Curtas-metragens, destinada a produções dos estados da Amazônia Legal; Outros Nortes, voltada a trabalhos e realizadores dos demais estados brasileiros; e Olhar Panorâmico, que apresenta uma seleção de títulos da região amazônica.

A programação contou ainda com a mostra não competitiva Olhinho, dedicada ao público infantojuvenil e aberta a produções de todo o país, além de obras convidadas pela curadoria.

A oitava edição do Festival Olhar do Norte recebeu 596 filmes inscritos. Foram 28 inscrições na Amazônia Longas, 188 na Amazônia Curtas, 325 em Outros Nortes e 55 na Olhinho.

Após as exibições presenciais, parte da seleção ganha uma janela digital por meio da parceria com a plataforma Itaú Cultural Play, que disponibilizará on-line os filmes das mostras de curtas amazônicos e panorâmicos até 12 de outubro.

articles.title: ‘Star Wars’: Jon Watts to Direct Next Movie for Lucasfilm
articles.summary: Simon Kinberg is writing the new trilogy that is said to be next episodes of the Skywalker Saga.
articles.body:
Even as Lucasfilm is deep in post-production on its next Star Wars movie, Star Wars: Starfighter , the next phase of a potential new Skywalker Saga is coming into focus.

Jon Watts, the director behind a trio of Tom Holland Spider-Man movies, is now attached to direct the first installment of the Simon Kinberg-penned trilogy. It is a return to the franchise for Watts, who previously co-created Star Wars series Skeleton Crew in 2024.

Kinberg has been working on writing a mystery trilogy since late 2024. The project is intended to act as the next chapter in what is referred to as the Skywalker Saga, the stories featuring the multi-generations of the Luke Skywalker family. The previous movies have been Episodes I through IX . The next one would be Episode X . Rey Skywalker, the Jedi played by Daisy Ridley in last trilogy released from 2015 and 2019, would appear in some capacity in the new trilogy.

Sources say the project is still in development and has not yet been greenlit by parent company Disney, although it seems to be project the furthest along the development track after Starfighter .

Starfighter is being directed by Shawn Levy and stars Ryan Gosling. The movie is expected to hit theatres May 27, 2027, coinciding with the 50th anniversary of Star Wars .

Watts is seen as a reliable choice for the franchise, which has occasionally, and would say famously, struggled with directors. After directing the indie thriller Cop Car , Watts was chosen by Marvel to helm the relaunch of the Spider-Man movies. The Tom Holland-starring movies, which included 2017's Homecoming , 2019's Far From Home , and 2021's No Way Home , became progressively bigger productions and bigger hits at the box office. Watts proved he could navigate the complexities of massive big-budget productions.

His post- Spider-Man work included the George Clooney-Brad Pitt-starring Wolfs , the high-profile misfire from Apple that upended its theatrical release and curiously announced a sequel that was never going to be made.

Watts co-created and co-wrote Skeleton Crew , the well-regarded but unfortunately not greatly seen series that starred Jude Law and brought an Amblin vibe to the Star Wars universe. Watts directed two episodes of the show, which also had a starry assemblage of helmers that included David Lowery, Lee Isaac Chung, Jake Schreier, Bryce Dallas Howard, and the Daniels.

Knight Edge Media broke the news of Watts' involvement.

articles.title: Kayadu Lohar says Srikanth Odela warned her ‘The Paradise’ role would be very different; recalls he called himself  ‘little mad’ director
articles.summary: Actress Kayadu Lohar, who rose to fame with the Tamil film ‘Dragon’ played the female lead in Nani and Srikanth Odela’s latest release, ‘The Paradise’.
articles.body: Actress Kayadu Lohar, who rose to fame with the Tamil film ‘Dragon’ played the female lead in Nani and Srikanth Odela’s latest release, ‘The Paradise’. The film has been performing decently at the box office but received a mixed response from the audience, with some viewers also expressing disappointment with Kayadu’s character.Recently, the actress opened up about how director Srikanth Odela narrated the character to her and warned her that it would be very different from her previous roles.Srikanth Odela called himself a ‘different’ directorDuring a conversation with Permit Room, Kayadu recalled her first narration with the ‘Dasara’ director. She said the director introduced himself as someone who works differently and warned her that she needed to be ready for his style.“He gave me a brief about himself. He said that I'm a very different director, a little ‘mad’, I don't have plans and all. So only if you are up for that game, let me know. And I was like yeah, fine with it, because I didn't know what was coming,” she said.Kayadu Lohar says the role was difficultThe ‘Funky’ actress added that she had confidence in the project because it was led by Nani and featured music by Anirudh Ravichander. She also knew Srikanth from his previous film ‘Dasara’.Kayadu said she initially wondered how “mad” Srikanth could actually be. However, she later understood what the director meant while working on the film.“So I thought to myself, yeah fine, how mad could ‘mad’ mean? It can't be that much. But now I've realized just how much it is! But... then he narrated the character to me. He told me that it will be very different from what you have done. It might be difficult also,” she recalled.‘The Paradise’ was released on September 24 and has received a mixed response from audiences and critics. Some viewers praised the film’s performances and technical aspects, while others raised concerns about the story and certain characters.According to the figures shared by trade analyst Sacnilk, the film had collected Rs 79.68 crore net in India by Day 4, with its India gross standing at Rs 94.37 crore. The Day 4 net collection was reported at Rs 3.28 crore as of this morning.The film had collected Rs 46.25 crore on Day 1, Rs 14.90 crore on Day 2 and Rs 15.25 crore on Day 3.Nani responds to the feedbackNani has also addressed the mixed response to the film. The actor said he welcomed the feedback and acknowledged the flaws pointed out by audiences and reviewers.“I have seen all your reactions and responses. I’ve received all your love and equally enjoyed your hilarious trolls. I’m heartwarmed by the way audience have owned the film, and also learnt from the flaws that critics and reviewers have pointed out. Thank you for everything is all I can say,” Nani wrote.He added, “We have made #TheParadise with a lot of blood and sweat to give you a unique experience, and it’s all yours to celebrate or judge.”The film also includes Mohan Babu, Sonali Kulkarni and Raghav Juyal in key roles.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Ranbir Kapoor loses his cool with paparazzi after ‘Ramayana’ event as he steps out with Alia Bhatt, Vicky Kaushal and Sanjay Leela Bhansali: ‘Bahut bol raha hai tu’
articles.summary: Mumbai witnessed a star-studded outing on Saturday night as Ranbir Kapoor, Alia Bhatt, Vicky Kaushal and Sanjay Leela Bhansali stepped out together
articles.body: Mumbai witnessed a star-studded outing on Saturday night as Ranbir Kapoor, Alia Bhatt, Vicky Kaushal and Sanjay Leela Bhansali stepped out together following a busy day of film-related appearances. With ‘Ramayana’ making headlines and the cast of ‘Love & War’ also grabbing attention, the group became a natural draw for the paparazzi waiting outside.The four stopped to pose for photographs, with the evening initially appearing to be a routine celebrity photo opportunity. However, as the group wrapped up and began leaving, a brief exchange between Ranbir and a photographer caught attention online.Ranbir Kapoor asks Sanjay Leela Bhansali to join the frameA video from the outing has surfaced online, showing Ranbir, Alia, Vicky and Sanjay posing outside a restaurant. Ranbir was dressed in an olive-green short kurta paired with black jeans, while Alia opted for a neon-green dress. Vicky was seen in a white shirt and black trousers.During the photo session, Sanjay appeared to step away from the frame as Ranbir, Alia and Vicky continued posing. Ranbir then asked the filmmaker to return and join them for the photographs, with the group eventually posing together.The mood seemed to shift as the group prepared to leave. While Ranbir was walking away, a photographer could be heard repeatedly calling out to him and asking him to pose with Alia and Vicky.Ranbir turned around and replied, “Bahut bol raha hai tu ha (You are talking a lot).”The brief exchange has since caught the attention of social media users, with the video being widely circulated online.What is known about 'Love & War'Ranbir, Vicky and Alia are set to share the screen in Sanjay Leela Bhansali’s ‘Love & War’. Details about the period drama have largely been kept under wraps, although reports have described it as a romantic war drama.The story is expected to revolve around Ranbir and Vicky’s characters, who are reportedly Indian Air Force officers, and Alia’s character, with their lives becoming intertwined against the backdrop of war. The film has been written by Sanjay Leela Bhansali and Ila Bedi Dutta and also features Supriya Pathak in a key role.Ranbir Kapoor has 'Ramayana' lined up nextApart from ‘Love & War’, Ranbir is also headlining Nitesh Tiwari’s ‘Ramayana’, which is being planned as a two-part theatrical release. The first instalment is scheduled to arrive during Diwali 2026, while the second part is expected during Diwali 2027.The film features an ensemble cast including Yash, Sunny Deol, Lara Dutta and Rakul Preet Singh. Promotions for the project have already begun, with Ranbir recently joining the cast and team for a media interaction in Mumbai.Sai Pallavi, Ravie Dubey, DNEG, Namit Malhotra and content creator MrBeast were among those associated with the event.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Johnny Walker had only 30-40% vision in one eye yet memorised eye chart to pass BEST test, son Nasirr Khan reveals his struggles from age 12
articles.summary: Johnny Walker is remembered for making generations of Hindi film audiences laugh, but behind that familiar comic persona was a childhood shaped by
articles.body: Johnny Walker is remembered for making generations of Hindi film audiences laugh, but behind that familiar comic persona was a childhood shaped by poverty, constant relocation and an extraordinary determination to survive. The legendary actor, whose real name was Badruddin Jamaluddin Kazi, began working when he was barely 12 or 13.His son, actor Nasirr Khan, recently opened up about those lesser-known chapters of his father’s life in a conversation with Vickey Lalwani. From selling ice cream and fruits to working at a bicycle shop, Walker took on several odd jobs before eventually becoming a BEST bus conductor. Even getting that job required him to find a way around a serious eyesight problem.He knew the eye test could stop him from getting the jobWalker had severely impaired vision in his left eye after an incident during his teenage years. According to Nasirr, the problem began when his father was around 14 or 15.“When he was around 14 or 15, he developed a problem with his left eye. The doctor gave him some eye drops and asked him to come back after 10 or 15 days. When he went back, the doctor wasn’t there; there was only a compounder. The compounder accidentally put ear drops in Daddy’s eye,” Nasirr recalled.The mistake reportedly caused permanent damage“As a result, he lost vision in his left eye. He could not see properly from that eye for the rest of his life. He could see only about 30 to 40 per cent with his left eye, and his vision deteriorated further as he grew older,” he said.Yet, when an opportunity to become a BEST conductor came his way, Walker refused to let the eyesight issue end his chances.“When he went for the conductor’s job, someone told him there would be a physical test. He knew that he would fail the eye test. So, on the day of the physical examination, he arrived at 8 am and memorised the entire eye chart before his test. He memorised it and then passed the physical,” Nasirr said.Childhood meant finding the next way to earnLong before the eye test, however, Walker had already learnt what it meant to earn a living.His family’s financial troubles began after his father, who worked as a mill manager, lost his job. The family moved from one place to another in search of employment, but things continued to deteriorate.“As a child, there was a point when his father was a mill manager and things were going well. Then his father lost his job. They moved from there to Indore in search of work. After some time, that job was also lost, and they moved somewhere else. The entire family kept moving from one place to another, but they could never settle down. Their financial situation kept getting worse,” Nasirr said.Walker eventually decided to leave school and start earning himself.“Daddy left school when he was 12 or 13 and started working. He began selling fruits and ice cream from a bicycle because his father was unable to find another job and could not earn money. He thought, ‘I have to do something. I have to try to earn some money so that the whole family can have two proper meals a day,’” he recalled.There was hardly a job he did not tryThe future comedian’s early working life had little connection with the glamorous world he would eventually enter. He simply kept moving from one opportunity to another.“Daddy used to sell ice cream, sell kite string, work at a bicycle shop, sell fruits and even shout slogans at fairs. There is hardly any job that Daddy did not do,” Nasirr said.He added, “Before he became a bus conductor, when he was 12, 13, 14 or 15 years old, he did all these jobs. He had lost everything at that point.”The family eventually reached Bombay, where Walker got an opportunity to work with BEST.“Then they came to Bombay. My grandfather had some contacts, so they asked if Johnny Walker could be given a job as a conductor with BEST,” Nasirr said.The bus conductor who found his way into filmsThe BEST job eventually became an unexpected turning point. While working as a conductor, Walker’s natural comic ability reportedly caught the attention of actor Balraj Sahni, who introduced him to filmmaker Guru Dutt. That connection changed the direction of his life.Walker got an opportunity to appear in ‘Baazi’ and gradually established himself as one of Hindi cinema’s most recognisable comic performers. He later featured in films such as ‘Pyaasa’, ‘CID’, ‘Mr. & Mrs. 55’ and ‘Madhumati’.What audiences eventually saw was a confident performer capable of turning even a small appearance into a memorable one. Behind that effortless humour, however, was the story of a boy who had left school at 12, worked several jobs to support his family, lived with limited vision in one eye and still found a way to build a career in cinema.Nasirr’s recollection offers a glimpse into the life of the man behind the laughter, long before Johnny Walker became a name synonymous with comedy in Hindi films.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.body: Kashmera Shah has publicly backed her 'maami' Sunita Ahuja following what appeared to be serious allegations made against her by Komal Rani Swarnkar in a recent note. The controversy erupted amid speculation about an alleged affair between Govinda and Komal Rani, his co-star in ‘Roopa’. Weighing in on the matter, Kashmera questioned how a co-star could possibly have insight into such private, personal details. She further noted that this marked the first time women in their family had been called 'murderers' for defending the men they love, and reaffirmed that she stands proudly by Sunita Ahuja, now and always.Kashmera Shah on keeping personal life privateIn a recent Instagram post, Kashmera talked about how she has always kept a clear line between her work and personal life over the years. She mentioned that even after working alongside many co-stars, she never confided in them about her private feelings or personal matters. While stopping short of naming Komal Rani directly, Kashmera seemed to question the dynamic between her and Govinda. Kashmera wrote, “Since the beginning of my career, 30 years and 50 films in total not “one co star" of mine knew anything about my personal life or feelings. The only person I told everything to was the person I married- Krushna Abhishek. I have never heard of such a bond in a work environment where a co worker knows such intimate details".Kashmera then addressed the criticism aimed at Sunita, noting that women who defend the people they love are often unfairly labelled. She further wrote, “I know I am a strong woman and I married into a family of strong women. We are often called RUDE OBNOXIOUS DOMINATING FOCUSSED SELFISH just because we look out for our families but this is the first time we are called “murderers”. So if every mother,wife,sister,aunt and their dogs are called murderers for protecting the “one man” that they love, be it the father, the husband,the brother, and the dog then so be it. I am proud that you are such a woman @officialsunitaahuja and I will always stand by you.”Komal Rani's note amid the controversyKomal Rani recently posted a note on Instagram, and while she stopped short of naming Govinda's wife Sunita Ahuja directly, she wrote, "Jo aurat apne hi pati ko salon se jaan se marne ki koshish kar rahi ho aisi auraton ki badduayen kisi ko nhi lagti. (The curses of a woman who has been trying to kill her own husband for years do not affect anyone.) Nobody ever can be a homebreaker in already broken house." The post followed a viral video from Dakshineshwar Kali Temple, in which Sunita was heard saying, "Mera ghar toot raha hai for no reason."Rani further added, “She seems to enjoy putting it on display in public. Is this really a pain or is it a carefully thought out conspiracy? To constantly mentally harass a man, stop him from working, force him to sit at home and waste away, isolate him completely and drive him to the point of death. I don’t think any good and devoted wife could treat her husband so terribly. Are women like this mentally unwell, or are they simply too clever for their own good, fully aware that what they couldn’t accomplish behind doors, they can achieve by going public and gaining people’s sympathy”.How the Govinda-Komal Rani rumours startedSpeculation about Govinda and his Roopa co-star Komal Rani Swarnkar first surfaced earlier this year, after the two were spotted together at Mumbai airport. Rumours gained further momentum when they were seen at public events together, including a visit to Mumbai's Lalbaugcha Raja.About Govinda and Sunita Ahuja's marriageGovinda and Sunita Ahuja got married in 1987 and have shared nearly four decades together as a couple. articles.title: Rob Lowe says he was ‘the only person happy’ after Will Smith slapped Chris Rock at Oscars; hoped incident would overshadow his own infamous 1989 Academy Awards performance
articles.summary: Actor Rob Lowe has opened up about one of the most infamous moments in Oscars history, his bizarre 1989 Academy Awards performance, and admitted that he
articles.body: Actor Rob Lowe has opened up about one of the most infamous moments in Oscars history, his bizarre 1989 Academy Awards performance, and admitted that he was actually relieved when Will Smith slapped Chris Rock during the 2022 ceremony.Speaking on SiriusXM’s Andy Cohen Live on Thursday, Lowe said he was “the only person happy” when Smith walked onto the Oscars stage and slapped Rock, because he believed the incident would finally take the spotlight away from his own long-running awards show controversy.“When Will Smith slapped Chris Rock, I was the only person happy. Because I was like, ‘Oh, good. So now that’s the worst moment in Oscar history,’” Lowe said.“But it turns out not really. Turns out I still am dragged, dragged every year.”Rob Lowe jokes that his Oscars blunder still haunts himLowe, 62, went on to joke that his infamous performance continues to be referenced whenever another awards show goes wrong.“This year even, I guess some people didn’t love some of the Emmys and they were like, ‘At least it wasn’t Rob.’ It’s like, guys, there should be a statute of limitations,” he said.The actor was referring to the opening number at the 61st Academy Awards in 1989, which he himself described as “the worst opening ever.”The performance saw Lowe perform an extended musical routine with actress Eileen Bowman, who appeared dressed as Disney's Snow White. The duo sang altered versions of popular songs, including a parody of “Proud Mary” featuring the line, “rollin’, rollin’, keep the cameras rollin’.”The unusual performance was widely criticised and subsequently became one of the most notorious moments in Oscars history.1989 Oscars performance sparked backlashThe fallout went beyond criticism from viewers and entertainment circles. Several prominent Hollywood figures, including then-former Academy President Gregory Peck, reportedly signed a letter condemning the ceremony.Disney also sued over the unauthorised use of its Snow White character.The controversy was particularly damaging for producer Allan Carr, who was behind that year's Academy Awards ceremony and whose Hollywood career was reportedly severely affected by the backlash.For years, the 1989 opening remained a reference point whenever discussions turned to the most awkward or controversial moments in Oscars history.Will Smith’s Oscars slap became another defining momentThat changed in 2022, when Will Smith shocked viewers around the world by walking onto the Oscars stage and slapping Chris Rock, who was presenting the Best Documentary Feature award.Rock had made a joke about Jada Pinkett Smith's shaved head, referencing the film G.I. Jane and saying, “‘G.I. Jane 2,’ can’t wait to see it.”Pinkett Smith, who has spoken publicly about living with alopecia, had shaved her head.Smith subsequently walked onto the stage and struck Rock before returning to his seat. He then shouted at the comedian, “Keep my wife’s name out of your f–king mouth.”The incident immediately became one of the most talked-about moments in Academy Awards history.Following the altercation, Smith was barred from attending Academy events, including the Oscars, for 10 years. The actor apologised to Rock the following day, writing on social media, “I was out of line and I was wrong.”Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.summary: La actriz y cantante, de 57 años, ha compartido un vídeo en sus redes sociales en el que aparece sin maquillaje mientras inicia su rutina de cuidado de la piel
articles.body: Jennifer Lopez ha vuelto a sorprender a sus seguidores, esta vez por una razón alejada de los escenarios y las alfombras rojas. La actriz y cantante se ha mostrado al natural y sin una gota de maquillaje en un vídeo publicado en sus redes sociales, en el que ha aprovechado para compartir su rutina de cuidado de la piel y reflexionar sobre los cambios que atraviesa en su vida personal. "Estaba a punto de comenzar mi rutina de cuidado de la piel, y estaba pensando en rutinas porque mis hijos se van a la universidad", ha explicado la artista al comienzo de la grabación. Los hijos de Jennifer Lopez, los gemelos Max y Oskar Muñiz, de 18 años, han emprendido una nueva etapa lejos de casa, algo que supone también un importante cambio para la intérprete. La artista estadounidense ha reconocido que este verano ha intentado aprovechar al máximo el tiempo junto a ellos antes de su marcha. Jennifer Lopez también ha bromeado sobre las consecuencias que los últimos meses han tenido sobre su piel. "Los viajes fueron una locura, y destrozaron mi piel", ha confesado mientras se disponía a comenzar su ritual de cuidado facial. Sin embargo, para la artista estas rutinas tienen una importancia que va mucho más allá de la estética. "Esas rutinas son las que realmente me ayudan a seguir adelante", ha asegurado. La cantante ha reconocido que la marcha de sus hijos le genera sentimientos encontrados y ha imaginado cómo afrontará los momentos de nostalgia cuando la casa esté vacía. "Creo que cuando se vayan, y esté aquí sentada, con el nido vacío, llorando, pensando en ellos y mirando sus fotos de bebés, estas rutinas son las que me van a mantener un poco cuerda", ha explicado. La artista también ha querido poner el foco en la parte positiva de esta nueva etapa. Jennifer Lopez ha confesado que se siente emocionada por ver a sus hijos comenzar una nueva etapa de sus vidas, aunque reconoce que para ella también supone afrontar una importante transformación personal. "Es un momento aterrador, es un momento de transición, un nuevo comienzo en muchos sentidos", ha señalado. Jennifer Lopez ha aprovechado además el vídeo para lanzar un mensaje a sus seguidoras y reivindicar la importancia de mantener pequeños hábitos cotidianos durante los periodos de cambio. "Mantener las rutinas, mantenerse hidratadas, ser felices, estar alegres y ser productivas", ha recomendado la estadounidense antes de finalizar la grabación.

articles.title: Hugh Hefner's 'most sexy' Playboy model reveals how Anna Nicole Smith changed her life
articles.summary: Sandra Taylor shares stories of dating Fabio, shooting romance novel covers and Dan Aykroyd buying her SAG card after her Playboy career launched.
articles.body: Anna Nicole Smith unknowingly transformed the life of the woman Hugh Hefner once called his "most sexy model." Sandra Taylor, who made hearts race as a Playboy cover girl during the '90s, is now the head sommelier at Allegiant Stadium, home of the Las Vegas Raiders. But long before then, her friendship with the 1993 Playmate of the Year changed the course of her life. Taylor recently appeared on Sports Illustrated Swimsuit model Kim Alexis' podcast, "Unexpired," where she reflected on her life and career. LARRY BIRKHEAD CELEBRATES DAUGHTER DANNIELYNN'S 20TH BIRTHDAY WITH RARE PHOTOS "I was friends with Anna Nicole Smith, and she was such a darling," Taylor recalled to Fox News Digital. "We shared two makeup artists. One was in New York, one was in LA. And they introduced us very, very early on to her coming here from Texas, and we became friends. She needed a place to stay when she first came out here." A visit to Smith on the set of "Naked Gun 33 1/3: The Final Insult" changed the course of Taylor's career. After Smith's makeup artist urged her to meet with Playboy during its 40th anniversary search, Smith encouraged her friend to go for it. The opportunity led Taylor to Playboy and launched a new chapter in her life. WATCH: SANDRA TAYLOR REVEALS HOW ANNA NICOLE SMITH LED HER TO PLAYBOY "It was my friendship with Anna Nicole Smith ... it led me right there," said Taylor. "I never, in a million years growing up, thought I would ever be in Playboy," she said. "It just seemed so out of the realm of reality. I was full speed ahead to be a mathematician just like my dad. ... I studied macroeconomics, microeconomics, statistics, differential equations, and I was a dream dancer." "I was only 19 years old when my dad passed away," she continued. "It was on my college campus at SUNY Purchase. He was walking with my mom, and he had a heart attack just out of the blue and passed away. And then I never went back to that campus again. Books in locker; never went back. Never looked back. I always used to joke, 'I wonder if my books are still in my locker,' because I never cleared it out. But after that, when he passed away, the math died along with him, and I just didn't want to do it anymore." After her father's sudden death, Taylor abandoned her plans to pursue math and embraced a career in modeling. Looking back, she remains grateful for her friendship with Smith, whom she credits with helping open the door to Playboy before Smith died in 2007 at 39. "I remember how sweet she was," said Taylor. "She was really, really a sweet girl and loved her son so much. She really wanted to be a great mom. She was really a sweetheart, just a really nice girl. I don't think she could hurt a fly." For Taylor, posing for Playboy was only the beginning. She said it led to a friendship with Hefner that lasted until his death in 2017 at 91. LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS "Even when you do the magazine, it doesn't end there," Taylor explained. "Hef opens up his home for years to come. ... Because I was good friends with Kimberley, his wife, I was able to fly on their jet. I was able to really experience him as a family man, and how kind he was, too. I loved his laugh. If I look back, his laugh to me was the most infectious, wonderful thing about him. And I miss him. I really think he changed the trajectory of things for me. I'm sure it closed some doors ... but I wouldn't change it for the world." Decades later, Taylor said she learned what Hefner thought of her Playboy photos. "You know Traci Bingham from 'Baywatch?'" said Taylor. "She had told me when she went in to discuss doing Playboy, it was right around the time my layout was [going] to press. She goes, 'I want to do a layout just like that! Who's that?' And he was like, 'Oh, this is Sandra Taylor. She's our most sexy model we've ever had.' I go, 'Why did you wait all these years to tell me that amazing piece of trivia? I would've loved to have known years ago what Hef thought about me.'" "I always knew he was so into blondes, like real blondes," said Taylor. "So to think he was a fan of my photos as well. I just thought he had to use diversity in the magazine. Brunettes, blondes ... every single walk of life you want to represent in the magazine. But I always thought he favored blondes. So, when she told me that, it was so beautiful. ... I was like, 'Traci, could you tell me that one more time?'" Becoming a sought-after model had plenty of perks for Taylor — like catching Fabio’s eye. WATCH: SANDRA TAYLOR RECALLS DATING FABIO, POSING FOR ROMANCE COVERS "Shooting the romance covers with Fabio was exactly what you would imagine it would be," said Taylor. "These elaborate wardrobes — the fan, the hair, everything. It was so wonderful. It was in New York. I met Fabio at this gym called the Vertical Club. He was so sweet. We dated a few times, and he was lovely. He said, 'Have you ever thought about doing a romance novel cover?' And I was like, 'No, but I would love to.'" GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE "I was on the yes train from the get-go," said Taylor. "I always was interested. I always had an open mind, and I always kept myself very interested in anything that came my way. ... I don't know how many romance novel covers we did together, but it was a lot. You shoot many, many in one [day]. So that was really fun. That was a great experience." As an actress, Taylor frequently worked with director Garry Marshall. She also appeared in projects with Steven Seagal, Robert De Niro and other Hollywood stars. "Steven Seagal was really kind to me," said Taylor. "He was a real gentleman to me. Every time I went to audition, and it was multiple times, there were more beautiful women. The rooms were just packed with beautiful women. I just braced myself. But he was so professional. I remember I wore my lucky pink Chanel suit. The first thing he said to me was, 'Oh, my wife has a suit similar to that.' He was just so chivalrous and kind to me." "And Dan Aykroyd, I remember he was incredibly generous too. He bought me my SAG card for my first movie. Dan was like, 'I would love to pay for that for you and one day be able to say that I bought you your SAG card.' That was a beautiful surprise. He was also very kind and welcoming. I'll never forget that." PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE Taylor's life today is "a little different," she said. articles.title: Bruce Campbell says Hollywood studios left ‘very sour’ taste after he was 'kicked out' of lead role
articles.summary: After a cancer diagnosis and decades in Hollywood, Bruce Campbell and wife Ida Gearon filmed "Ernie & Emma" entirely in their home state of Oregon.
articles.body: Bruce Campbell is taking a chainsaw to the Hollywood playbook. The "Evil Dead" star is ditching the traditional studio system for "Ernie & Emma," his new independent film that puts him firmly in the driver's seat after decades of navigating Hollywood — and after one early studio experience left a bad taste. "The first studio film I ever did, I got kicked out of the lead," Campbell told Fox News Digital. "The movie was re-edited, retitled and never came out. So, the taste in my mouth from studios is very sour." KEVIN SORBO BLASTS HOLLYWOOD 'BLACKLISTING' OF CONSERVATIVES AS 'SEVENTH GRADE MEAN GIRLS' CULTURE That experience stuck with the cult-favorite actor, who said he has long wanted to make a project without studio executives calling the shots. "It was time to be unbridled in my life," Campbell said. WATCH: BRUCE CAMPBELL SAYS HOLLYWOOD STUDIOS LEFT 'VERY SOUR' TASTE IN HIS MOUTH The decision carries extra weight following Campbell's cancer diagnosis, which he disclosed in March. Campbell said earlier this month on "The Adam Carolla Show" podcast that doctors had given him an estimated five years to live, but he remains focused on treatment and continuing his work. The actor wrote, directed, produced and stars in "Ernie & Emma," which he made independently with his wife and longtime partner, Ida Gearon. For Campbell, the project represents a return to the kind of creative freedom he experienced early in his career with "The Evil Dead." TAYLOR SHERIDAN TAKES SWIPE AT LOS ANGELES AFTER BUILDING TV EMPIRE FROM TEXAS "The very first movie we did, ‘Evil Dead,’ was the only other movie I've ever done free and clear of the studio system," he said. articles.title: Jordi Évole, sobre la política de vivienda del Gobierno: "Si el Gobierno liderado por el PSOE especula con la Ley de Vivienda, se acabó"
articles.standfirst: El periodista ha lanzado un comentario crítico en redes sociales
articles.summary: El periodista ha lanzado un comentario crítico en redes sociales
articles.body: La situación de Maricarmen, la mujer de 87 años que fue desahuciada de la vivienda en la que había vivido durante más de siete décadas, ha vuelto a situar el problema de la vivienda en el centro del debate público. Su caso ha provocado movilizaciones en Madrid y ha llevado al Gobierno a plantear nuevas medidas para intentar responder a situaciones similares. El Sindicato de Inquilinas e Inquilinos de Madrid convocó este sábado una manifestación que partió de la Puerta del Sol. Posteriormente, cientos de personas permanecieron en la Puerta del Sol durante la noche en una acampada para reclamar cambios en materia de vivienda. En paralelo, el Gobierno de Pedro Sánchez ha anunciado que trabaja para llevar este martes al Consejo de Ministros un Real Decreto Ley sobre vivienda. El propio presidente se dirigió a Maricarmen a través de su cuenta de X y pidió a los grupos parlamentarios que hagan "un último esfuerzo" para que la norma pueda ser convalidada posteriormente en el Congreso. En medio de esta situación de diferencia de opiniones y contraposiciones, el periodista y experto Jordi Évole también se ha pronunciado públicamente. El periodista ha utilizado sus redes sociales para valorar el momento político generado alrededor del caso de Maricarmen y de la futura norma sobre vivienda. "Llegó el match point. Este sí que es el momento clave. Si el gobierno liderado por el PSOE especula con la Ley de Vivienda, se acabó", escribió Évole en una publicación en X durante la noche del sábado. Un mensaje muy crítico de cara al gobierno central, y que pone de manifiesto el descontento general que existe en este momento en España. Sus palabras llegan después de una jornada marcada por las movilizaciones en Madrid y mientras el Gobierno prepara el decreto que pretende llevar al Consejo de Ministros este martes.

articles.title: Quote of the day by Gary Oldman: 'Wanting to be a good actor is not good enough,' a powerful life lesson on ambition and finding your inner fire
articles.summary: Gary Oldman shares invaluable insights on ambition and the journey to greatness in acting, emphasizing the importance of internal drive over mere desire to be good.
articles.body: Being good at something is usually the goal. But for Gary Oldman, that was never really enough. Known for giving stellar performances and noteworthy characters from Sid Vicious and Count Dracula to Commissioner Gordon and Winston Churchill, Oldman has a very specific idea about what it takes to become great at something.During an interview with Richard Covington for Salon, published on July 9, 1997, Oldman spoke about teaching acting students and the difference between simply wanting to be good and genuinely wanting to be great. He described that ambition as something that has to come from inside you.Today’s quote of the day by Gary Oldman reads: “Wanting to be a good actor is not good enough. You must want to be a great actor. You just have to have that. It’s not something you can wear like a coat. It’s in you. It’s like a furnace.”What does the quote by Gary Oldman mean?Oldman was not simply telling young actors to chase fame. His idea was more about how badly you want to improve at something. In the Salon interview, he described that drive as being like a furnace. You cannot put it on for a performance and take it off afterwards. If the ambition is really there, it becomes part of how you approach the work.That is a pretty useful way of looking at ambition in general.Being “good enough” can become an easy stopping point. You reach a certain level, people are happy with your work, and there is no obvious reason to push yourself further. But if you genuinely want to be great, there is always something else to learn.And Oldman's own career reflects that restless approach. He has moved between theatre, independent films and huge Hollywood productions, often taking on very different kinds of characters rather than sticking to one safe formula.How is the quote by Gary Oldman relevant today?There is nothing wrong with wanting to be good at what you do. But if you are serious about building a career, eventually you have to ask yourself whether you are simply trying to finish something or actually trying to get better at it.That could apply to almost anything. Writing, acting, filmmaking, business, sports or even a college subject. You make something. You look at it. You notice where it could have been better. Then you try again.The internet can make success look very sudden. Someone becomes a successful creator, writer or entrepreneur and it can seem as if they simply got lucky. What is harder to see is all the work that happened before anyone was paying attention. Oldman's “furnace” is really about that internal push. You cannot fake it forever.Early life of Gary OldmanGary Leonard Oldman was born on March 21, 1958, in New Cross, London. He grew up in a working-class family and developed an interest in acting while he was young.He eventually studied at the Rose Bruford College of Speech and Drama and went on to work extensively in British theatre before making the move into film.Oldman's early career was not built around glamorous Hollywood roles. He worked with respected British directors and theatre companies, gradually developing a reputation for throwing himself completely into difficult characters. That intensity became one of the things audiences came to associate with him.How did Gary Oldman rise to fame?Oldman first gained major attention for playing Sid Vicious in the 1986 film 'Sid and Nancy'. The role put him on the international radar and showed just how far he was willing to go for a performance.He followed it with roles in films including 'Prick Up Your Ears', 'JFK', 'Dracula', 'True Romance' and 'The Fifth Element'. In the 2000s, a new generation of audiences knew him as Sirius Black in the 'Harry Potter' films and Commissioner Gordon in Christopher Nolan's 'The Dark Knight' trilogy.He later won the Academy Award for Best Actor for playing Winston Churchill in 'Darkest Hour'. But the interesting thing about the 1997 Salon interview is that Oldman was already questioning his own creative drive at the time. He told Covington that he felt the “fire” to act had gone and admitted that acting could sometimes become boring after years of doing it.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more.
