articles.title: Habitus explores the brahminisation of traditional practices: Kiran KR
articles.summary: Kiran KR’s short documentary Habitus, selected for the Malayalam Short Documentary section, examines how familiar cultural practices and ancient
articles.body: Kiran KR’s short documentary Habitus, selected for the Malayalam Short Documentary section, examines how familiar cultural practices and ancient traditions are gradually reshaped by a changing social order.Speaking to us, the director says the 20-minute documentary was made as part of his fourth-semester project at KR Narayanan Film Institute. “It discusses how non-Brahmanical practices and customs are getting Brahminised. It is a study of how this is increasingly happening,” he says.His inquiry began at home. “My father is the priest at a nearby temple. I noticed the changes from there and observed the changes that had happened over the past 15 years. My observation was that the practices had become Brahminised. I have also explored how this affects ordinary people,” he shares.For the documentary, Kiran focused on two temples as case studies. “I understood that many temples have undergone changes. I took two case studies. One is the temple where my father is a priest, and the other is a temple in Kollengode, Palakkad. We went there and filmed. During the filming, we understood that the temple had been taken over by a group based in Thiruvananthapuram. We also explored how these changes lean towards right-wing politics,” he says.This is not Kiran’s first selection at the festival. His short film was selected in the campus section in 2020, and Habitus marks his fourth visit to the festival. “It is one of the bravest and strongest documentary and short film festivals in the state. The most prominent filmmakers in the country want to screen their work here. Being able to screen my own documentary here is fortunate. I am excited about the result,” he says.On this year’s selection, he adds, “According to my understanding, the selection is good, and I am looking forward to watching the works I haven’t seen yet and getting to know everyone.”Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: I had no idea that people from the South have so much love for me: Dhvani Bhanushali
articles.summary: Singer Dhvani Bhanushali, who recently performed in Thiruvananthapuram, says the warmth of the audience made the experience particularly special.
articles.body: Singer Dhvani Bhanushali, who recently performed in Thiruvananthapuram, says the warmth of the audience made the experience particularly special. “I loved performing here. My heart was so happy seeing so many people. The sheer love I got made me reel throughout the performance,” she says.The Psycho Saiyaan singer also visited the Sree Padmanabhaswamy Temple before taking the stage. The temple visit, she shares, left her awestruck. “I saw Vishnu ji’s idol and it’s the most surreal moorthi. The three doors, and how we get to see his face and the whole story behind it. I was just really amazed and I got to take that energy on to the stage. I would love to come here again,” she says.Dhvani says she is pleasantly surprised by the response she receives from audiences in South India. “I had no idea that people from the South have so much love for me. But when I go to cities like Bengaluru, they are so responsive and loving. I performed in Chennai, too, a week after I performed in Thiruvananthapuram. I have an upcoming show in Bengaluru in the first week of November. I am grateful that I have carved out a space in their hearts for me. Every time I perform in the south, I hope I can return the love and make audiences happy,” she gushes.The singer describes the song Vaaste, which she recorded with Nikhil D’Souza, as "career-defining". “Vaaste is always going to be fresh for me. It is a song that gave me my career. It is a song that gave me a lot of love. I still don’t understand what audiences connect with in the song; it’s probably the innocence of the time. They attach their nostalgia and childhood to it. Somehow I also became a childhood crush for so many of them. That makes me feel good," she says and adds, "I was 21 and today, I am 28, and it’s just so surreal that a song can still connect after six-seven years and have a place in people’s hearts.”While playback singing has been an enriching experience, Dhvani says independent music gives her greater creative freedom. “Independent work fulfills me a lot more because I get to tell the whole story exactly the way I want with the creative minds I work with. Playback is a different journey. I have done less of it, but I am really happy to have had that enriching experience. But independent music is something that I like to do more. People know me because of my work in this space,” she says.Her new EP, Feels, is deeply personal, drawing from different relationships and aspects of her life. “It is about my life — my relationships, where I come from, and so on. I started with a song about my dad because he holds a beautiful, special place in my heart and, like most daughters, I felt I really need to tap into that emotion,” she shares.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: 'Avengers Endgame: Encore' scores USD 86 million debut weekend; Marvel film nears 'Avatar' record to become highest-grossing film of all time
articles.summary: Seven years after becoming the second-highest grossing film ever, 'Avengers: Endgame' returned to the No.
articles.body: Seven years after becoming the second-highest grossing film ever, 'Avengers: Endgame' returned to the No. 1 spot at the box office in a victory lap for Marvel and an appetizer for the upcoming blockbuster 'Avengers: Doomsday'. The film, that re-released with the title 'Avengers Endgame: Encore', not only managed to regain the box office crown, but also set itself up to regain the box office crown from 'Avatar'.The rerelease grossed USD 26 million over the weekend and another USD 60 million overseas, according to studio estimates Sunday. 'Avengers: Endgame', which earned a worldwide haul of USD 86 million over its debut weekend, now has a global box office estimate of USD 2.88 billion. This is just USD 40 million short of USD 2.92 billion total collection of 'Avatar' (2009).'Avengers Endgame: Encore' among most successful rereleasesThe film, which grossed USD 2.8 billion in 2019, was put back into theaters with several new end-credits scenes and an introductory thank you to fans from Robert Downey Jr. and Chris Evans.Among rereleases, only the 1997 release of 'Star Wars: A New Hope' (USD 35.9 million) and the 2011 repeat of 'The Lion King' (USD 30.2 million) have opened higher than 'Endgame' in domestic cinemas.'Avengers Endgame: Encore' tops crowded box officeHollywood has increasingly turned to rereleases in recent years to take advantage of holes in the release schedule. But The Walt Disney Co. rerun, billed as 'Endgame: Encore', came out on top on an especially crowded weekend in theaters. Three well-reviewed new releases - A24's Primetime', with Robert Pattinson; Paramount Pictures' 'Heart of the Beast', with Brad Pitt; and Universal Pictures' 'Forgotten Island' - all landed in theaters.'Resident Evil' makes USD 23.3 million debutSecond place, though, went to Zach Cregger's reboot of 'Resident Evil'. The Sony Pictures release followed up its above-expectations debut with USD 23.3 million in its second weekend. In two weeks, the video-game adaptation has grossed USD 103.5 million in U.S. and Canadian theaters.'Heart of the Beast' scores USD 20 million openingIn a close race for third place, 'Heart of the Beast' came out just ahead of 'Primetime' with an estimated USD 20 million from 3,435 theaters. Directed by David Ayer, the film stars Pitt as a retired veteran who must trek through the Alaskan wilderness with his combat dog after a plane crash. It added $30.1 million in international theaters.Robert Pattinson drives 'Primetime' salesBut the opening for 'Primetime' was more impressive. 'Heart of the Beast' cost $82 million to produce, making its path to profitability challenging. 'Primetime', starring Pattinson as 'To Catch a Predator' host Chris Hansen, was made with a modest budget of USD 15 million and it opened in 500 fewer theaters.Yet 'Primetime', buoyed by strong reviews and buzz out of the Venice Film Festival, debuted with USD 19.2 million. For Pattinson, who also starred this year in A24's 'The Drama' and Universal's 'The Odyssey', the strong performance showed the actor's drawing power with Gen Z audiences.Some 69% of ticket buyers for 'Primetime' were under the age of 30. Gen Z has emerged as the most regular moviegoing demographic, fueling hits this year like 'Obsession' and 'Backrooms'. 'Primetime' is directed by 30-year-old documentarian Lance Oppenheim, who co-directed the much-anticipated Elizabeth Holmes documentary, 'You Can See Everything', due out next month.'Forgotten Island' fails to make a mark'Forgotten Island', from DreamWorks Animation, had a hard time standing out. The film, which cost USD 80 million to make, opened in fifth place with a disappointing USD 12.8 million domestically. In 31 overseas markets, 'Forgotten Island' also didn't make much of a dent, grossing USD 7.8 million internationally.Universal will hope family audiences catch up to the movie that landed the weekend's best CinemaScore (an "A") and the best reviews (94% fresh on Rotten Tomatoes). 'Forgotten Island', directed by Joel Crawford and Januel Mercado, is about two friends who get stranded in a mystical world.The confluence of releases added up to a historically good September weekend in theaters. According to Rentrak, ticket sales were up 58.5% from the same weekend last year. articles.title: 'Home Improvement' star says Patricia Richardson got 'tired' of fighting for sitcom
articles.summary: Taran Noah Smith reveals Patricia Richardson fought to keep "Home Improvement" realistic as new writers pushed scripts in a different direction.
articles.body: "Home Improvement" star Taran Noah Smith is shedding new light on why the hit 1990s sitcom came to an end. The 42-year-old former actor was seven-years-old when he landed the role of Mark Taylor, the youngest son of Tim "The Tool Man" Taylor (Tim Allen) and his wife Jill Taylor (Patricia Richardson) in 1991. The sitcom, which was based on Allen's stand-up comedy persona, centered on Tim, a television host known for his home improvement show, "Tool Time," and his family life with Jill, Mark and older sons Brad (Zachery Ty Bryan) and Randy (Jonathan Taylor Thomas). 'HOME IMPROVEMENT' STAR JONATHAN TAYLOR THOMAS ARRESTED FOR ALLEGED PUBLIC INTOXICATION, RESISTING DEPUTY "Home Improvement" became one of the highest-rated shows of the '90s and ran for eight seasons and aired 204 episodes. However, the show concluded in 1999 after Richardson declined to return for a proposed ninth season. During a recent appearance on Tom Scharpling and Julia Vickerman's podcast "Outgrown" podcast, Smith reflected on his time starring on the show and weighed in on the reasons behind Richardson's departure. TIM ALLEN SAYS HE 'NEVER REALLY WANTED' TO BE A DAD AND OPENS UP ABOUT SOBRIETY AND FATHERHOOD REGRETS Smith recalled that Richardson joined the cast as Jill just days before the pilot was taped after producers replaced Frances Fisher, the actress originally cast as Tim's wife, during rehearsals. "When they brought Patricia in, there was just a much better chemistry," he said. "And she had her own kid. She had just given birth to twins, and she had one older kid who was about my age. She really brought a lot more of a realistic mom energy to her, and she fought throughout the whole show to keep the show more realistic." "She would tell the writers, ‘A mother would never say this,’ and get them to change it," he added. Smith said he "definitely" agreed with Richardson's input though he acknowledged that he and the show's other child stars weren't really involved in conversations about the script. "They'd do a run-through of the script on Monday and then the kids would go to school usually, and they would continue to discuss the script," he said. Smith recalled that there were creative disagreements on set after a new creative team replaced the show's original writers and producers. ROSEANNE BARR HASN’T SPOKEN TO TV SISTER LAURIE METCALF SINCE SHOW’S CANCELLATION "The original creators only did the first couple seasons, and then they moved on, and they brought in a whole other group of writer/producers," he remembered. "Those guys, very few of them had kids, and the show kind of started to go in a different direction, at least the scripts we'd get on Monday." "It was really Pat, the mom, who fought the good fight to make it more realistic because oftentimes it would just be something that was very out of character just to sell a joke, just to set up a joke," he continued. "It's like, ‘Wait, this is not what the characters are about.’" ROSEANNE BARR CALLS FORMER CO-STAR A 'BRAINWASHED BIGOT' AFTER HE SAID REBOOT WAS 'RIGHTFULLY CANCELED' Smith speculated that Allen was reluctant to appear overly controlling after witnessing what happened on another sitcom, "Roseanne." "Roseanne," which became an instant hit after it premiered in 1988, was created by "Home Improvement" co-creator Matt Williams. Like "Home Improvement," Roseanne was built around its star's stand-up comedy voice and persona. However, Barr clashed behind-the-scenes with producers and writers, including Williams, over the direction and tone of the show. The tensions between the two led to Williams leaving after the first season. Barr later gained more influence and was credited as a creator in later seasons. ‘THE OFFICE’ STAR JENNA FISCHER EXPOSES THE GRUELING REALITY THAT FORCED HER OFF TV "I think Tim was overall maybe a bit worried about being a tyrant because the same creators created ‘Roseanne,’ and Roseanne took over the show and fired the creators, fired everybody," Smith recalled. "Actually, all our camera crew had been fired in one day from ‘Roseanne’ and came over to us. So, Tim was always, I think, more hands-off with that, not wanting to be tyrannical, which meant that it was a lot more on Pat to push." "That's one of the reasons why the show ended up eventually ending, because she was just tired of it, of having to fight to make it realistic all the time," he continued. JODIE SWEETIN SHARES SHOCKING 'FULL HOUSE' RESIDUAL CHECK AMOUNT DESPITE SHOW'S MEGA SUCCESS "And Tim was getting far more money than she was," Smith added. "That was her actual way of stopping. She said she'd do a ninth season if she got paid the same amount as Tim, knowing they wouldn't do it." Smith's recollection of why Richardson left "Home Improvement" echoes what the actress has said for years about her experience on the show and the reasons for her departure. During a May 2024 interview with the Los Angeles Times, Richardson recalled that the creators emphasized the importance of the character of Jill and her relationship with Tim. "When I took the job, they said it wasn’t meant to be the Tim Allen show. It was meant to be our show," she said. "I’ve always said, I don’t want to play the thankless wife." Richardson recalled having creative disagreements with male writers over how Jill would react to specific situations, remembering one instance in which she was told, "Pat, it’s not like we don’t understand women. We’re married to them." The actress, who earned four Primetime Emmy Award nominations for her performance as Jill, told the LA Times that she made the decision to leave the show. Richardson told the LA Times she decided during the eighth season that it would be her last, citing a desire to spend more time with her children after her divorce and her belief that the sitcom had run its course, pointing to Jonathan Taylor Thomas' departure and declining ratings. GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE The actress also felt that Disney failed to recognize her creative contributions to the series, saying she helped shape her character and storylines but was denied a producer credit, even as Allen became an executive producer. "I told everybody, there’s not enough money in the world to get me to do a ninth year. This show is over. It needs to end," Richardson recalled. LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? articles.body: 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day' is nearing the end of its theatrical run. The film, which rewrote several records at the box office, following an extended theatrical run, is reportedly set to arrive on digital platforms on October 6.'Spider-Man: Brand New Day' worldwide box office collectionsThe Tom Holland-led Marvel film, directed by Destin Daniel Cretton, opened in theatres on July 31 and has continued to draw audiences well into its ninth weekend.
